about: Lighting setups for the cinematographer. 'category' says which guide a row comes from: 'cinematic' rows are the quick chooser of docs/research/cinematic-lighting-guide.md; 'interview' rows are the studio interview setups of docs/research/studio-interview-lighting-guide.md. Pick the row whose intent matches the shot, then copy setup, quality, direction, color_temp, practicals and the finish default into light_look. 'stays_dark' is what the card must say falls into darkness. 'do_not_use_when' lists moods the setup is wrong for. 'low_key' marks setups whose setup text triggers the flat_light guards (negatives.json applies_when); the loop row is left false because its broad version is open and bright, and the dressed-set interview row is left false because its set never goes black. 'board_url' is the Cosmos study board with reference frames. Interview rows also carry 'people' (a number, or [min, max]), 'rig' (the practical numbers for a shot list or crew brief: key source, side, angle, height, distance_m and kelvin; fill or negative fill (a black panel that soaks up bounce); rim; background stops_vs_face and subject_distance_m; camera a_mm, b_mm, aperture and eyeline; contrast_ratio) and 'small_kit' (the same look with 2-3 lights). Ranges are [min, max]. The rig is for planning and crew notes, not for the prompt. Direction words are a starting point: always name the side (frame-left, frame-right, behind, above).

setups.name: Rembrandt
setups.direction: 45-degree key, high, frame-left
setups.practicals: one lamp or window in background
setups.finish: natural skin with pores and fine lines, faint shadow-side bounce but no fill
setups.stays_dark: the far side of the face except the small triangle; the background falls to near-black
do_not_use_when: beauty shots that need open skin

setups.name: Butterfly / Paramount
setups.direction: key on lens axis, above, angled down
setups.practicals: none, or overhead fixture implied
setups.finish: natural skin with pores and fine lines, backlit flyaway hairs
setups.stays_dark: cheek hollows and eye sockets; the background is dark or one halo

setups.name: Split
setups.direction: side light at 90 degrees, eye height
setups.practicals: one lamp, window or blind slats
setups.finish: natural skin with pores and fine lines, slight underexposure
setups.stays_dark: the unlit half of the face merges into a black room

setups.name: Loop, broad, short
setups.direction: 30-45 degree key, slightly high
setups.practicals: window or lamp off-frame
setups.finish: natural skin with pores and fine lines, faint shadow-side bounce but no fill
setups.stays_dark: the shadow side of the face (short version); the background is dark or a soft gradient
do_not_use_when: the face must sit in a pool or silhouette
a graphic half-face is wanted (use split)

setups.name: High key
setups.direction: large frontal or overhead
setups.color_temp: one temperature throughout (cool white or warm cream)
setups.practicals: ceiling panels, big window
setups.finish: true-to-life colour, natural skin with pores and fine lines
setups.stays_dark: nothing large; only costume and small objects carry true black

setups.name: Low key
setups.direction: single high key or backlight
setups.color_temp: amber tungsten, or warm spark on cool ambient
setups.practicals: blinds, street lamp, bulb
setups.finish: crushed blacks with no milky shadows, natural skin with pores and fine lines
setups.stays_dark: most of the frame: shadow sides and the set fall to black, except one bright opening

setups.name: Window light
setups.direction: side light 60-110 degrees
setups.practicals: the window itself, sun patch on wall
setups.finish: natural skin with pores and fine lines, lived-in set with dust and worn surfaces
setups.stays_dark: the room away from the window and the foreground nearest camera
do_not_use_when: the scene is at night with no window source
a crisp graphic shadow is wanted (use hard sun or split)

setups.name: Backlight / rim
setups.direction: back light or contre-jour, one side
setups.practicals: sun, window, lamp or stage light behind
setups.finish: backlit flyaway hairs, peach fuzz catching the rim, soft veiling flare
setups.stays_dark: the side of the subject facing the lens; dark backgrounds stay crushed black
do_not_use_when: the face and expression must read clearly
dialogue close-ups that need both eyes

setups.name: Motivated practicals
setups.direction: from the practical's side
setups.practicals: desk lamp, screen glow, pendant
setups.finish: soft lamp halos that shrink with distance, natural skin with pores and fine lines
setups.stays_dark: everything away from the practicals: 50-70% of the frame in shadow

setups.name: Golden hour
setups.direction: contre-jour or low side, 0-10 degrees up
setups.practicals: none (the sun)
setups.finish: soft veiling flare, backlit flyaway hairs
setups.stays_dark: the shadow side of the subject in silhouette versions; shadows stay deep but not crushed
do_not_use_when: a scene that must cut with midday or night shots

setups.name: Blue hour
setups.direction: sky behind or window side
setups.practicals: streetlamp, table lamp, lit distant windows
setups.finish: navy shadows with detail, soft lamp halos that shrink with distance
setups.stays_dark: the ground and buildings in navy shadow; subjects against the sky go to silhouette
do_not_use_when: faces must read in detail without a lamp

setups.name: Night exterior mixed colour
setups.direction: side or top from street sources
setups.practicals: street lamps, neon sign, car headlights
setups.finish: uncorrected practical colours, crushed blacks with no milky shadows
setups.stays_dark: 60-80% of the frame: streets, skyline and the subject's shadow side
do_not_use_when: unmotivated cyberpunk colour with no signs in shot

setups.name: Overcast
setups.direction: top light (exterior) or window side (interior)
setups.practicals: none
setups.finish: lived-in set with dust and worn surfaces, natural skin with pores and fine lines
setups.stays_dark: nothing large; true black only in dark clothing or deep forest

setups.name: Hard sun / dappled
setups.direction: high side, 60-90 degrees
setups.practicals: blinds, leaves, window grid
setups.finish: natural skin with pores and fine lines, slight underexposure
setups.stays_dark: the shadow bands and the shade; never lift them to see the face

setups.name: Firelight / candlelight
setups.direction: low, from below and side
setups.practicals: candles, lantern, torch, campfire
setups.finish: gentle flame flicker, brown-black firelit shadows
setups.stays_dark: most of the frame; only the pool around each flame holds midtones

setups.name: Top light
setups.direction: overhead 60-90 degrees
setups.practicals: pendant lamp, ceiling fixture
setups.finish: crushed blacks with no milky shadows, natural skin with pores and fine lines
setups.stays_dark: eye sockets, the room beyond the pool and the background

setups.name: Documentary interview: soft key, dark background
setups.setup: low-key documentary interview lighting, one large soft key
setups.quality: soft wraparound key, deep shadow falloff, no fill
setups.direction: short side (the side the subject looks towards), 30-60 degrees off the eyeline, 30-45 degrees above eye height, angled down
setups.color_temp: key 4300-5000K, warm tungsten practical 2700-3000K, faint cool 6500-8000K accent
setups.practicals: a dimmed warm table lamp in the back third of frame, a soft slash of light on the back wall, optional low cool LED strip on the floor
setups.finish: natural skin texture with pores and fine lines, large round catchlight in both eyes, gently lifted blacks
setups.stays_dark: the shadow side of the face falls into a smooth dark; the room sits 2-4 stops under the face, broken only by the lamp and the slash
do_not_use_when: a series that must look clean and even

key.source: 120-150cm deep octa or parabolic, or a 4x4-6x6 diffusion frame, gridded
key.height: 30-45 degrees above eye height, angled down

rig.fill: none; a black 4x4 floppy 1-1.5m off the shadow cheek (if fill is needed, a far bounce 2-3 stops under the key)
rig.rim: optional small LED behind on the key side, only to pull dark hair off black

background.notes: warm practical plus a slash or pool 1-2 stops under the face; dark textured wall; never a pure black void

camera.eyeline: interviewer beside the A lens on the shadow side; B on the same side of the eyeline, 20-30 degrees further round

rig.contrast_ratio: high: no fill, the far cheek falls to a smooth dark

small_kit: Key: 300-600W COB in a 120cm gridded deep octa, short side, about 45 degrees, slightly above eye level, 1.2m away
Negative fill: black 4x4 or V-flat on the shadow side, plus a flag between the key and the wall
Background: a 2700K dimmable table lamp and/or a small barn-doored LED raking a slash across the wall

setups.name: Classic three-point interview
setups.quality: large soft key, gentle falloff on the far cheek, low fill
setups.direction: key on the short side, 30-50 degrees off the lens, centre 20-40cm above the eyes, angled down; rim high behind on the opposite side
setups.color_temp: daylight 5600K key (4300-5000K on a mixed location), warm practicals 2700-3200K, cool backdrop against warm skin
setups.practicals: a small accent lamp or hidden tube off to one side, kept 1-2 stops under the face
setups.finish: natural skin texture with pores and fine lines, soft catchlights at 10 or 2 o'clock
setups.stays_dark: the far cheek sits 1-1.5 stops under the near side; a darker zone stays right behind the head

key.source: 90-120cm gridded deep octa or parabolic, or a 4x4-6x6 grid-cloth frame
key.height: centre 20-40cm above the eyes, angled down

rig.fill: often none: a black floppy 1-1.5m off the shadow cheek; for a brighter corporate look, a bounce near the lens at 1/4 to 1/8 of the key
rig.rim: small Fresnel or 60-120W COB 120-160 degrees from camera, opposite the key, 2.2-3m high, flagged off the lens

background.notes: coloured seamless lit on its own (evenly for a series), or a real room with the ambient pulled down

camera.eyeline: interviewer beside the A lens, subject slightly off-axis; B 20-40 degrees away in angle

small_kit: Key: 300-600W COB in a 90cm gridded parabolic, 40 degrees on the short side, 1-1.2m away, 30cm above the eyes, lens side flagged
Rim: 60-150W COB or small Fresnel, high, 130-150 degrees behind on the opposite side
Background: a small gridded or snooted LED pool on the wall 2m behind, or a practical

setups.name: High-key white studio interview
intent: social vertical with room for captions
setups.quality: soft overhead wraparound light, low contrast, gentle shadows under brow and chin
setups.direction: one parabolic per subject on a boom, 30-45 degrees off the nose towards the eyeline, 1-1.5m above head height, tilted down; soft top fill overhead
setups.color_temp: daylight 5600K throughout, key and cyc matched (or warmed to 4300-5000K for creamy white)
setups.practicals: none; booms and stands may show on purpose in the wide
setups.finish: natural skin texture with pores and fine lines, slightly warm skin, no shine on the forehead
setups.stays_dark: nothing large; only wardrobe, chairs and a black solid on the far side of the face hold shape

key.source: 120-150cm parabolic or deep octa per subject, on a boom
key.angle: 30-45 degrees off the nose towards the eyeline
key.height: 1-1.5m above head height, tilted down 30-45 degrees

rig.fill: overhead lantern or space light 3-4m high plus the white floor; black floppies above and beside each key, a black solid on the far side for shape
rig.rim: rarely; a small gridded top-back light only when hair blends into the cyc

background.notes: cyc lit by its own units, never by the keys; about level for light grey, with a soft halo between the chairs

camera.eyeline: at least three cameras: a centred locked-off wide, singles from beside the other person's shoulder 15-30 degrees off the eyeline

rig.contrast_ratio: low: the white floor bounces fill back up

small_kit: Key: 120cm parabolic on a boom, about 45 degrees to the side the subject faces, 1m above the eyes
Background: a COB or 60cm softbox behind the subject aimed at the paper, flagged off the subject, pushing the paper 1-1.5 stops over the face
Optional: a china ball as top fill, or a white 4x4 bounce; grey rug if faces go flat

setups.name: Low-key black void interview
setups.quality: single soft key, chiaroscuro falloff to black, small Rembrandt patch on the shadow cheek
setups.direction: key on the short side, 45-70 degrees off the lens, 20-40 degrees above the eyeline; for wides, one hard source high at three-quarter back
setups.color_temp: key 4300-5000K, neutral black void (never gelled), any rim matched or slightly cooler
setups.practicals: none; at most a soft pool of light on the floor around the chair
setups.finish: natural skin texture with pores and fine lines, crushed blacks with no milky shadows, soft catchlight in both eyes
setups.stays_dark: the shadow side of the face goes near-black; the background sits 4-6 stops under and nothing behind the subject reads
do_not_use_when: subjects in all-black clothes with no rim

key.source: 4-5ft octa or 4x4 grid-cloth frame with a 40-degree grid and a black skirt

rig.fill: none, or a bounce or very low LED near the lens 2-3 stops under; a black 4x4 close on the shadow side is required
rig.rim: optional faint rim from a 1x1 LED or barn-doored Fresnel behind; leave out for the purest void

background.notes: black duvetyne or velvet, no background light; any texture comes from key spill only

camera.eyeline: interviewer tight beside the lens on the far side from the key (or an Interrotron, a device that lets the subject look into the lens); wide C-cam 24-35mm of the chair in its pool

small_kit: Key: 300-600W COB in a 90-120cm gridded parabolic, 60 degrees off-axis on the short side, about 30 degrees up, 1-1.2m away
Edge (optional): 60-100W LED, high three-quarter back, at low output
Black duvetyne or the darkest wall 2-3m behind, all room lights off, negative fill and a grid

setups.name: Dressed set with practicals (lamps, shelves, bokeh)
setups.setup: dressed-set interview lighting, one large soft key with warm lamps behind
setups.quality: soft key from high above the face, set lit in pools with dark gaps, never flat
setups.direction: key 20-45 degrees off the lens on the side the subject faces, hung 30-50cm above the eyeline, tilted down; over a table, one disc centred above
setups.color_temp: key 4300-5000K, lamps and shelf LEDs 2400-3000K, one cool or magenta accent
setups.practicals: 1-3 dimmed warm lamps (Edison bulbs, sconces, shelf LED tape) at different depths, beside the head, never growing out of it
setups.finish: natural skin texture with pores and fine lines, creamy round bokeh from the bulbs, warm mids with neutral skin
setups.stays_dark: the gaps between the lamp pools; the set sits 1.5-3 stops under the face but never goes fully black

key.source: 120-150cm parabolic or octa, or a 1.2-2m round diffusion, gridded when walls are close
key.height: 30-50cm above the eyeline, tilted down 30-45 degrees

rig.fill: usually none; tabletop and walls bounce enough, negative fill if a light wall flattens the face
rig.rim: optional small gridded strip 120-150 degrees behind at low level; the practicals often do it

background.notes: real dressed set in pools; lamps dimmed to 25-60%; one accent colour at most; key a few hundred kelvin cooler than the lamps

camera.eyeline: A slightly off-axis with a lamp in the empty side; B a wide of the set; optional OTS on 35-50mm

small_kit: Key: 200-300W COB in a 90-120cm gridded parabolic, high, about 30 degrees off-axis, 1-1.2m away
Set: a roll of dimmable warm LED tape, or two small RGB tubes hidden behind shelves or a plant
Practicals: a shaded table lamp and a paper or Edison lamp with dimmable 2700K bulbs at different depths

setups.name: Coloured background wash and gels
setups.setup: coloured background wash, neutral soft key on the face
setups.quality: soft clean key, saturated colour on the wall only
setups.direction: key on the short side, 30-45 degrees off the lens, 20-40 degrees up; colour units 2-4m behind the subject, aimed only at the wall
setups.color_temp: white balance locked to a 5600K key; saturated teal, magenta, deep blue or amber gels on the background
setups.practicals: an RGB tube, neon sign or logo in frame to motivate the colour
setups.finish: natural skin texture with pores and fine lines, clean natural skin tones with no colour spill
setups.stays_dark: the edges of the colour field; the subject's shadow never lands in the middle of a wash

rig.fill: low bounce from the camera side, or none plus negative fill for a moodier look
rig.rim: optional small gridded source in the second colour, 120-150 degrees behind at head height, kept off the cheek

background.notes: its own lighting zone: a hard gelled circle, even RGB uplights, or one deep room colour; two hues at most

camera.eyeline: off-axis to the interviewer on the key side, subject centred on the colour pool; creator setups go on-axis to the lens

small_kit: Key: 120-150cm octa or 90cm parabolic on a COB at 5600K, 35-45 degrees on the short side, gridded
Background: a COB with a Fresnel or projection attachment and a gel, or an RGB panel, low behind the subject and aimed at the wall
Optional: an RGB tube as a coloured rim or practical

setups.name: Window-style soft side light in studio
setups.setup: window light from the side, studio built
setups.quality: very large soft source, gradual falloff across the face
setups.direction: side light 60-90 degrees off the lens on the side the subject faces, top edge at or above head height, 1-2m from the face
setups.color_temp: daylight 5000-5600K key, warm practicals 2700-3200K, slightly cool shadows
setups.practicals: 2-3 dimmed warm lamps in the background, optional bright sheer curtain on the key side
setups.finish: natural skin texture with pores and fine lines, one set of catchlights, no hard nose shadow
setups.stays_dark: the far cheek, held by a black solid; the background sits 1-2 stops under

key.source: 6x6-8x8ft diffusion frame (4x4 minimum) with a COB pushed through, or a 5-7ft parabolic feathered across
key.height: top edge at or above head height, bottom near seat height

rig.fill: none for moody work; a black 4x4 close on the opposite side; for corporate, a white bounce near camera lifting the far cheek 1/2 to 1 stop
rig.rim: optional faint back edge from the window side, 120-150 degrees from camera

background.notes: dressed room in deep green, navy or timber, flagged from the key

camera.eyeline: interviewer beside the A lens on the key side; B 30-45 degrees off on the opposite side

small_kit: Key: 300-600W COB through a 4x4 or 6x6 frame (or a 120-150cm parabolic), 70-90 degrees to one side, centre just above eye height, 1-1.5m away, with a black 4x4 or V-flat opposite
A warm practical or small LED tube in the background, dimmed
Optional: a gridded 60-100W LED as a low back kick, or skimming the back wall

setups.name: Podcast and multi-person studio
intent: host and guest at a table
setups.setup: low-key podcast lighting, one matched soft key per seat overhead
setups.quality: soft wraparound light on each face, pool of light on the table, room falls off
setups.direction: each key overhead and in front of its seat, 20-35 degrees off that person's eyeline, aimed down 30-40 degrees; in a two-hander the keys cross-key from the other side
setups.color_temp: every key the same, 4300-5600K; uplights 2700-3200K plus one purple, teal or cyan accent
setups.practicals: warm uplights, cyan or purple shelf strips, pendants or lamps, dimmed separately
setups.finish: natural skin texture with pores and fine lines, boom-arm mics in shot, warm mids with slightly cool shadows
setups.stays_dark: the room beyond the table pool and the floor around the table; the set sits 1.5-3 stops under the faces
do_not_use_when: a set that must look like a real home

key.source: 1.2-1.5m octa or Light Dome per seat on a pipe or boom, identical model, power, height and Kelvin
key.side: short (cross-keyed from the other person's side)
key.height: 1-1.5m above head height, aimed down 30-40 degrees

rig.fill: usually none; tabletop and the other key's spill fill it; black flags on the outside of each seat and a floor cutter
rig.rim: optional shared round source behind the table between two facing people, with low front fill

background.notes: dark textured room lit on its own in pools; floor around the table kept dark

camera.eyeline: 3-4 cameras: a wide master, a cross single per person 20-40 degrees off-axis; eyelines to the other person, never the lens

rig.contrast_ratio: moderate; add white only if the contrast tops about 3:1

small_kit: Keys: two 90-120cm gridded octas on booms, one per person, about 1m above head height, in front, angled down 35 degrees, same model, power and Kelvin
Background: a small COB or tube with a gel or RGB raking the back wall from low, or two practical lamps
Black flag outside each seat; for 3-4 people, one big overhead softbox or 4x4 frame plus a gridded panel on the main speaker
